pr_title: Fix JNI emitSignal with one or more parameters
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/39018

Code borrowed from JNI `GodotLib.calldeferred` [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f69760b4befd7348c443960b84dd5f4e1d372e17/platform/android/plugin/godot_plugin_jni.cpp#L112-L133).

~**Disclaimer:** I have not quite figured out _why_ this fixes the issue, so I'd be glad if anyone knows and is able to explain. :)~
pr_comments: @pouleyKetchoupp Makes sense, thank you for the explanation! :)

issue_context.title: JNI emitSignal is broken
comments: @timoschwarzer Can you provide the arguments you were passing to the `emitSignal` call that caused the crash.
Just a simple String is enough. e.g. `emitSignal("my Signal", "Hello World")`

I don't know if it makes a difference, but I am running the app in release_debug mode (launched directly from the editor by clicking the Android run button in the top right corner) and in my signal handler GDScript function I just print the string.

```
func on_my_event(arg):
    print(arg)
```
I also tried some other types supported by `_jobject_to_variant` (Dictionary etc.) and they result in the same crash.

review_comments:
I'm thinking that a static assert here would make it safer since the number of arguments is hardcoded:
`static_assert(VARIANT_ARG_MAX == 5);`
I'll make a separate PR for this to add this to `call_deferred`, too.
This condition should use brackets to follow our c++ coding rules (better add clean code even if it was copied from somewhere else).
